{{Current events|year=2019|month=07|day=24|content=

<!-- All news items below this line -->
;Armed conflicts and attacks
*[[Somali Civil War (2009–present)|Somali Civil War]]
**A suicide bomber detonates inside the office of [[Mogadishu]]'s mayor [[Abdirahman Abdi Osman]], killing six government officials. Osman is seriously injured in the attack and his condition is critical. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-africa-49100440 (BBC)]

;Business and economy
*[[Boeing 737 MAX groundings]]
**[[Boeing]] reports its largest-ever quarterly loss, of {{usd}}2.9 billion, as a result of the grounding of its [[Boeing 737 MAX|737 MAX]] series, with the company saying that it could halt its production. [https://www.theguardian.com/business/2019/jul/24/boeing-reports-largest-ever-quarterly-loss-following-737-max-grounding (''The Guardian'')]

;Health and environment
*[[July 2019 European heat wave]]
**Highest-ever temperatures are recorded in [[Germany]] (at 40.5°C or 104.9°F), the [[Netherlands]] (at 39.2°C or 102.5°F), and [[Belgium]] (at 38.9°C or 102.0°F). [https://twitter.com/DWD_presse/status/1154116338002157570 (''Deutscher Wetterdienst'')], [https://www.theguardian.com/world/2019/jul/24/summers-second-heatwave-set-to-break-records-across-europe (''The Guardian'')]

;Politics and elections
*[[Premiership of Theresa May]], [[Premiership of Boris Johnson]]
**[[Theresa May]] visits Queen [[Elizabeth II]] at [[Buckingham Palace]] to officially resign and recommend her replacement as [[Prime Minister of the United Kingdom]]. [https://twitter.com/chrisshipitv/status/1154029884252930048/photo/1 (Royal Communications)]
**[[Greenpeace]] protesters block [[The Mall, London|The Mall]], the drive to Buckingham Palace, holding up Prime Minister-designate [[Boris Johnson]] on his way to visit the Queen. [https://www.theguardian.com/uk-news/live/2019/jul/24/boris-johnson-prepares-to-enter-downing-st-and-name-cabinet-theresa-may-prime-minister-live-news (''The Guardian'')]
**Johnson is asked by the Queen to form a government, making him the 55th Prime Minister of the United Kingdom. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/live/uk-politics-49073992 (BBC)]
**Multiple cabinet members resign on the day of Johnson's ascension to premiership, or in the days preceding it, in response to Johnson's politics and views on [[Brexit]], including [[Philip Hammond]], [[Jeremy Hunt]], [[David Gauke]], [[Sir Alan Duncan]], [[Rory Stewart]], [[Anne Milton]], and [[David Lidington]]. [https://www.theguardian.com/uk-news/live/2019/jul/24/boris-johnson-prepares-to-enter-downing-st-and-name-cabinet-theresa-may-prime-minister-live-news (''The Guardian'')], [https://www.ft.com/content/8c7f06e4-ad52-11e9-8030-530adfa879c2 (''Financial Times'')], [https://www.thetimes.co.uk/article/hammond-leads-wave-of-resignations-qcf6brskw (''The Times'')]
*[[Secretary-General of the European Commission]] [[Martin Selmayr]] is appointed as EC representative in [[Austria]] from November 1 on. [https://www.politico.eu/article/martin-selmayrs-new-job-the-eus-man-in-vienna/ (''Politico'')] [https://www.dw.com/en/eu-commission-shifts-top-civil-servant-martin-selmayr-to-vienna/a-49732350 (''Deutsche Welle'')]
*[[Annegret Kramp-Karrenbauer]] is sworn in as [[List of German defence ministers|German defence minister]]. [https://www.dw.com/en/kramp-karrenbauer-sworn-in-as-german-defense-minister/a-49727370 (''Deutsche Welle'')]
